note: 11 claims: 9 confirmed, 1 corrected, 1 unverified; the org-restriction gap is now fixed, but the guide still misstates callback matching by saying a single callback URL has wildcard matching on by default, when the docs limit that to apps that had one before August 3, 2026.

rows.composio: Same path, personal account or organization
rows.ours: Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App; personal account or an organization you administer
rows.provider: Same path; you can create it under your account or any organization you administer

rows.claim: How many callback URLs an OAuth app takes
rows.ours: Up to 10, added with Add callback URL
rows.provider: "You can enter up to 10 callback URLs." Composio's guide is out of date here

rows.changed: partly fixed; misstates who has wildcard on and omits exact-match rule
rows.claim: How the callback URL is matched
rows.composio: GitHub and the app must agree on the exact redirect destination
rows.ours: A single callback URL has wildcard matching on by default; turn it off unless needed. Exact rules otherwise unconfirmed
rows.provider: Wildcard matching is a per-callback-URL setting. Only apps that had a single callback URL before August 3, 2026 have it on; it is not stated as a default for new apps. With it off, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL. Disable it unless you absolutely need it

rows.ours: Expire user access tokens on by default: 8-hour access token, 6-month refresh token; keep it on and handle refresh
rows.provider: "Expire user access tokens is enabled by default." Access token expires after eight hours, refresh token after six months without use

rows.claim: offline_access scope gives an expiring token and refresh token
rows.ours: Yes: add offline_access to get an expiring token plus a refresh token
rows.provider: Requesting offline_access opts an individual sign-in into an expiring token and a refresh token

rows.ours: PKCE (code_challenge) strongly recommended; sent on the authorize request. S256 method not stated
rows.provider: code_challenge is strongly recommended; method must be S256, plain is not supported

rows.claim: Limit on OAuth apps per owner
rows.ours: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps
rows.provider: "A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps."

rows.composio: Don't put secrets or internal URLs in the visible fields
rows.ours: Use only public information in the app name and description
rows.provider: "Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public. Avoid using sensitive data, such as internal URLs"

rows.claim: Organizations can block third-party OAuth apps
rows.ours: Restrictions on by default for new organizations; members must request owner approval before the app reaches org data
rows.provider: "When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default." Members request owner approval; unapproved apps lose API access to private org resources

rows.composio: Enable it only for headless or constrained devices; the browser flow is usually enough
rows.ours: Tick Enable Device Flow only if you need it
rows.provider: Enable Device Flow only if the app will use the device flow to identify users

rows.claim: The client secret is shown only once
rows.composio: GitHub shows the client secret only once
rows.ours: Not covered (only says generate a client secret on the app page)
rows.provider: Not stated on the creating, authorizing or modifying-an-OAuth-app pages re-read in round 2, so the docs can't decide it
